Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : Let the Supplementary-Affidavit do form part of the main application.

2. Today is fixed for passing necessary order.

3. This is an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

<u>4. It has submitted before us that the petitioners have not come up with this Writ Petition for quashing the criminal proceedings pending against them in the Courts below; rather they have come up with the instant Writ Petition for protection of their fundamental rights as guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution and form arbitrary and malafide actions of the police personnel by way of filing fictions criminal cases namely, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 38 dated 16-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/ 149/186/353/307/332/333/109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 316 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 23 dated 11-9-2018 under sections 1451147/149/186/353/307/332/333/109/ 114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 25 dated 12-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/149/186/353/307/332/333/ 109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 26 dated 12-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/149/186/353/ 307/332/333/109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 31 dated 14-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/ 149/186/353/307/332/333/109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Mirpur Model Police Station Case No. 56 dated 15-9-2018 under section 15(3) of the Special, Powers Act, 1974 read with sections 4/5/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 against the petitioners and others. As the petitioners have not come up with the instant Writ Petition for quashing the proceedings of the cases pending against them in the Courts below and as a reference to Annexure-D' to the Supplementary-Affidavit, that is to say, paper-clipping of 'The Daily Jugantor' dated 24-9-2018 positively indicates that the Inspector-General of Police had already alerted the Police Headquarters for safeguarding the image of the police in filing cases against various persons who are allegedly dead, sick and away from the Juntry, 1 think, a Rule Nisi may be issued in the following terms:</u>

5. Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents 'to show cause as to why the allegedly arbitrary and malafide actions of the police officers currently being executed under the control and supervision of the respondents upon filing of the aforesaid purported fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and other indefinite number of people belonging to various different political parties/groups as evidenced by Annexure-'A' series to the Writ Petition should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondents should not be directed to take appropriate legal actions against the police officers who were involved in the lodging of those alleged malafide and fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and others and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

6. However, the Investigating Officer; are at liberty to carry out the investigation of the criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others in accordance with law.

7. The Inspector-General of Police Head-quarters, Police Station Shahbagh, Dhaka (respondent No. 2) is hereby directed to take steps to monitor and enquire into the alleged aforesaid fictitious and malafide criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others with different Police Stations of Dhaka Metropolitan City and submit a report to this Court by filing an Affidavit-in-Compliance within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. 8. The Rule is returnable within 4(four) weeks from date.

9. The petitioners are directed to put in requisites for service of notices upon the respondents by registered post as well as through usual process within 3(three) working days, failing which, the Rule shall stand discharged.

10. Put up the record on 17-12-2018 for passing necessary order.

Ashraful Kamal J: আমি মাননীয় জ্যেষ্ঠ বিচারপতি জনাব মইনুল ইসলাম চৌধুরী মহোদয়ের রুল ইস্যুর আদেশটি শুনলাম। আমি তাঁর প্রতি শ্রদ্ধা রেখে দরখাস্তকারীগণের অত্র দরখাস্ত দায়ের করার ন্যূনতম কোন কারণ না থাকায় তথা প্রাথমিকভাবে বিচারের কোন বিষয় না পাওয়ায় তাঁর রুল ইস্যুর আদেশের সহিত একমত হতে না পেরে তথা ভিন্নমত পোষণ করে দরখাস্তটি প্রাথমিক শুনানীতে সরাসরি প্রত্যাখান করছি।

১২. দরখাস্তকারীগণের দরখাস্ত পর্যালোচনা করলাম। দরখাস্তকারীগণের এবং বিজ্ঞ অ্যাডভোকেটগণের যুক্তিতর্ক বিস্তারিতভাবে শ্রবণ করলাম এবং তা যথাযথভাবে মূ্ল্যায়নসহ বিবেচনা করলাম।

১৩. অত্র রীট পিটিশন নিষ্পত্তিতে গুরুত্বপূর্ন বিধায় দরখাস্তকারীগণ রীট পিটিশনে যে বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেছেন তা নিয়ে অবিকল অনুলিখন হলোঃ

"1. The petitioners are law abiding citizen of Bangladesh. All the petitioners are legal practitioners and are practicing law regularly before both the Divisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh. They are members of Bangladesh. Supreme Court Bar Association. The petitioner No. 1 is a Senior Advocate and former president of Supreme Court Bar Association for 4 consecutive terms and was also elected as vice-chairman of Bangladesh Bar Council for 2 consecutive terms. He is the vice-chairman of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). The petitioner No. 2 is an Advocate and is the vice-chairman of BNP. He was Cabinet Minister for Youth and Sports and he was also served as the State Minister for Ministry of Education and Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. The petitioner No. 3 is also an Advocate and served as an Additional Attorney-General for Bangladesh. He is also a vice-chairman of BNP. The petitioner No. 4  is an Advocate and a former president of Dhaka Bar Association. He is the law  secretary of BNP All the petitioners have been falsely entangled in various criminal cases, which are currently pending. 2. The petitioners are conscious of their duty as politicians and citizens in consonance with Article 21 of the Constitution to ensure the observance of the Constitution and the law of Bangladesh and to ensure the prevention of illegal and unconstitutional encroachments upon the civil rights of the indefinite number of people and citizens of Bangladesh. The petitioners are interested in the welfare of the Republic and also aware of the fundamental rights enshrined in the Part 111 of the Constitution in general and in Articles 27, 33, 35, 36, 37, 38 and 39 of the Constitution in particular whereby all citizens are entitled to equal protection of law and which prohibit taking any action detrimental to the life, liberty, body, reputation or property of any person except in accordance with law. As democratic politicians and practicing lawyers of the Supreme. Court of Bangladesh, the petitioners, having sufficient interest and being aggrieved by the impugned actions, is filing this Writ Petition under Article 102 of the Constitution.

3. The writ petition is filed by the petitioners in their capacity as concerned, affected and aggrieved persons to protect the  national interest of Bangladesh being its democratic character having the best ride of law and independence of judiciary and to ensure the interest of indefinite number of people of Bangladesh and to uphold the Rule of Law by way of public interest litigation. The petitioners being committed to the welfare of the Republic and to ensure that the Rule of Law is upheld and to protect the public interest and as a public good spirited and concerned person brings this action pro bono publico in respect of matters set out herein. The petitioners are aware that all powers in the Republic belong to the People, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected under, and by the authority of this Constitution and that the Constitution is as the solemn expression of the will of the people, the Supreme Law of the Republic, and if any law and/or actions are 'inconsistent with this Constitution that other law and/or actions, to the extent of the, inconsistency, shall be void.

4. This writ petition is also maintainable in view of the latest guidelines given in the case of National Board of Revenue vs Abu Saeed Khan reported in 18 BLC (AD) 116 inasmuch as it has been brought before, this Hon'ble Court as a public interest litigation challenging the blatant abuse and misuse of power violating the directions of law in general and direction of the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in particular given in the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63.

5. The Respondent No. 1 is Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs; Respondent No. 2 is Inspector-General of Police; Respondent No. 3 is Commissioner, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No. 4 is Deputy Commissioner of Police, Ramna Zone, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No. 5 is Deputy Commissioner of Police, Detective Branch, North Zone, Office of Detective Branch; Respondent No. 6 is Additional Deputy Police Commissioner, Ramna Zone, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No. 7 is the Officer-in-Charge, Ramna Police Station, Dhaka; Respondent No. 8 is Officer-in-Charge, Paltan Police Station, Dhaka; and Respondent No. 9 is the Officer-in-Charge, Shahbagh Police Station.

6. The addresses of the parties mentioned in the cause title are their correct addresses and all notices may be served upon them in the said addresses.

7. The petitioner impugns herein this Writ Petition the arbitrary and malafide  actions of the Respondents executing through police officers under their control and  supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal  cases against the petitioners and other indefinite number of people who belong to different political groups than the government, which is evident from different newspaper reporting including the Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Nayadiganta and Manab Zamin published on several dates In September 2018. The petitioner further prays for an order of direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in the lodging of arbitrary, malafide and fictitious lodging of cases.

8. It transpires from the record maintained by BNP that in last 20 days (between 1-9-2018 and 20-9-2018) as many  as 3,736 cases have been filed against 3,13,130 known and unknown number of persons who belong to BNP and its alliance all over Bangladesh. Such cases are no doubt based on fictitious and concocted stories which have been filed by the Respondents under their supervision having malicious intention to harass, detain and control the opposition activists ahead of the ensuing parliamentary election scheduled to be held on any date between October 2018 and 9th January 2019. The reports supporting the aforesaid statements of the petitioners, published in different newspapers, amongst others the Daily Prothom Alo dated 5-9-2018 and 12-9-2018 and the Daily Nayadiganta dated 19-9-2018 and a report dated 20-9-2018 obtained from the office of BNP are annexed hereto and marked as Annexure-A series.

9. That it is stated that several newspaper reports also suggests that the police have filed some cases out of their blue design against dead persons, persons having severe health conditions, persons admitted into intensive care unit of various hospitals and clinics, persons who had gone for performing Hajj and so on. For instance (i) in the Daily Prothom Alo, a news report has been published with a caption “পুলিশের মামলায় আসামী মৃত ব্যক্তি ও প্রবাসীরা”; (ii) in jagonews 24.com, a news report has been published with a caption “মামলার প্রধান আসামী মৃত ব্যক্তি;

(iii) in Daily Ittefaq, a news report has been published with a caption “খুলনায় পুলিশের মামলায় মৃত ব্যক্তি আসামী”; (iv) in Daily Naya Diganta, a news report has been published with a caption “মৃত ব্যক্তি নাশকতা মামলার আসামী। রেহাই পাচ্ছেন না বিদেশে অবস্থানকারীরাও”; (v) In Daily Poriborton, a news report has been published with a caption   “বিএনপির মৃত নেতার নামে ২ মামলা”; (vi) In Daily Subarno Bhumi, a news report has been published with a caption “ঝিনাইদহে মৃত ব্যক্তিকে আসামী করলো পুলিশ”; (vii) In Daily Prothom Alo on 9-9-2018, a news report has been published with a caption “মৃত ব্যক্তিকে ককটেল ছুড়তে দেখেছে পুলিশ”; (viii) In Daily Manab Zamin dated 10-9-2018 a news report has been published with a caption “মৃত ব্যক্তিকে আসামি করে পুলিশের মামলায় তোলপাড়”;  (ix) In Daily Jugantor dated 15-9-2018 and 19-9-2018, a news reports have been published with a captions “আজগুবি মামলায় ভুতুড়ে আসামি and আশুগঞ্জে গায়েবী মামলায় মৃত ব্যক্তিও আসামি (x) In Daily Inquilab dated 20-9-2018, a news report has been published with a caption “হাজতী প্রবাসী ও মৃতরা সরকার উৎখাতে জড়িত”; The online printed copies of such reports are annexed hereto and marked as Annexure-B series.

10. That the petitioners have been  subjected to victims of such malicious actions  of the Respondents inasmuch as so far as  many as 7 cases have been filed against all of them ill different police stations. The petitioners have obtained anticipatory bail from the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in all the 7 cases, being Paltan PS Case No. 23 dated 11-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 25 dated 13-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 26 dated 13-9-2018. Paltan PS Case No. 31 dated 15-9-2018. Paltan PS Case No. 38 dated 17-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 38 dated 16-9-2018 and Mirpur Model PS Case No. 56 dated 16-9-2018. It appears from the FIR of all the 7 cases that the time, manner and articulation of the story are identical and any man of ordinary prudence can understand that all the FIRs are predesigned and those are made like a prescribed form and are used upon inserting some fictitious facts as and when required. Photocopies of the FIR of all the cases and bail granting orders are annexed hereto and marked as ANNEXURE-C series.

11. That it is stated that it is now well known to all concerned at home and abroad that the government and Bangladesh Awami League have prepared a blue design to retain their power through another farcical election and the summary of the said blue design can be presumed from their recent actions, which may be articulated in the following terms:

A. To keep the BNP Chairperson in jail until the election is over under any circumstances;

B. To convict the BNP acting Chairperson in 21 August case to demoralize the BNP supporters and to malign and defame them internationally;

C. In addition to the above two tasks, they are also preparing to deceive the global society to show that they are ready to hold a moderately free election. But under the veil, they have asked the puppet police to make sure that the grass-roots of BNP and its alliance are fragile through the bundles of cases against them and to cause delay in obtaining bail in mechanical manners;

D. In order to execute plan 3 above, the police administration has been given verbal instructions to file several cases against leaders and workers of BNP and its alliance in every constituency and accordingly, all the active members in poling centre wise are made accused in order to prevent them from being available for election campaign and selection of poling agents;

E. As part of the assignment mentioned in plan 4 above, fictitious cases like sedition, arms, ammunition, conspiracy etc. are being filed even where no iota of incidents were found to have occurred;

F. There is also verbal instruction upon the judicial magistrates not to grant bail in

these types of cases though they are fully authorized to grant bail and, as such, once someone is arrested, it takes around 3-4 months to get bail after completing higher judicial process. Thus, if any political activist is arrested now in such factious cases, he will not get bail at least before January 2019, i.e. he will only get bail after the elections; G. Police is receiving bribes from the activists of BNP and its allies under co-ercion and threat of custodial, extra-judicial killing and enforced disappearances;

H. The intellectuals/civil society members have been kept under threat of section 57 of the ICT Act, 2006 so that they cannot express their opinion;

I. To make the activists of BNP and its alliance, their family members and supporters financially crippled so that they cannot spend money during movements/election;

J. To purchase lobbyists by spending their looted money to pacify the western world; and

K. If peaceful movement/demonstrations/ procession is organized by BNP, Sheikh Hasina's public and private cadres will burn vehicles and kill people and will shift the liability upon BNP and its alliance.

12. That it is stated that the recent Rations and treatments of the respondents treating the activists of BNP its allies critics of Government are ex-facie discriminatory against the people belong to the shadow of the Government. Such actions of the Respondents, being suppressing the opposition activists and voices upon lodging cases against them, restricting their movement, freedom of speech, freedom of conscience, freedom of association, are nothing but a violation of the fundamental rights of indefinite number of people, which offends the provisions of Articles 27, 31, 33, 35, 36, 37, 38 and 39 of the Constitution inasmuch as the people opposing Government's fascist activities, bad governance, suppression, etc are being subjected to discriminatory treatment, their right to life and liberty are at risk, their freedom of movement, freedom of association, freedom of assembly, freedom of speech are shrinked. It is further stated that the purported cases filed against the petitioners and indefinite number of people in recent limes having malice in law and fact have been instituted by misusing the provision of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (CrPC) having arbitrary and malafide intention to keep them away from the election process or to do certain election engineering under the blue design of the Government and, as such, those are liable to be declared to have done without any lawful authority and of ho legal effect.

13. The actions of the Respondents suffers from gross malice in fact and malice in law as can be equated with the principle set out in the case of Dr Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 201, inasmuch as the impugned actions of the respondents taken against the petitioners and an indefinite number of people demonstrate the wrongful act done intentionally without just cause in total disregard of the principle of ride of law, denial of fundamental rights and ignorance of the ratio settled in different cases by our apex court, including the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST and others reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63."

14. অত্র রীট পিটিশনের ১ ও ২ নং দরখাস্তকারী বাংলাদেশ ন্যাশনালিষ্ট পার্টি তথা বিএনপির ভাইস চেয়ারম্যান এবং ৩ নং দরখাস্তকারী আইন সম্পাদক। দরখাস্তকারীগণের অভিযোগ প্রতিপক্ষগণ স্বেচ্ছাচারী এবং উদ্দেশ্যমূলকভাবে পুলিশ কর্মকর্তাদের ব্যবহার করে, নিয়ন্ত্রন করে এবং তত্ত্বাবধানের মাধ্যমে অত্র দরখাস্তকারীগণসহ বিএনপির নেতা কর্মী এবং সমর্থকদের বিরুদ্ধে মিথ্যা মামলা এবং আজগুবি মামলা দায়ের করে আসছে। বিগত ইংরেজী ১-৯-২০১৮ তারিখ হতে ২০-৯-২০১৮ তারিখ পর্যন্ত ৩,১৩,১৩০ জন বিএনপি কর্মীর বিরুদ্ধে ৩৫৩৬ টি মিথ্যা মামলা দায়ের করা হয়। আগামী সংসদ নির্বাচনকে মাথায় রেখে প্রতিপক্ষগণ দরখাস্তকারীগণসহ বিএনপি নেতা কর্মীদের হয়রানী করার উদ্দেশ্যে উল্লেখিত সাজানো, মিথ্যা এবং আজগুবি মামলা দায়ের করে চলেছে। উপরিল্লিখিত অবস্থাধীনে দরখাস্তকারীগণ নিম্নরুপ প্র্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করে।

"A Rule Nisi calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the arbitrary  and malafide actions of the Respondents executing through police officers under their control and supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and other indefinite number of people who belong to different political groups than the government, which is evident from different newspaper reporting including the Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Nayadiganta and Manab Zamin published on different dates in September 2018 (Annexure-A series) shall  not be declared to have been done without  any lawful authority and of no legal effect and  as to why the Respondents shall not be  directed to take appropriate legal actions  against the police officers who are involved in  the said lodging of arbitrary, malafide and  fictitious of cases.

Pending hearing of the Ride, restrain the Respondents from lodging any further case against the petitioners and other opposition activists and also direct the Respondent No.  to form an independent enquiring committee of 7 members comprising representatives from UN Human Rights Committee, Human  Rights Watch, Amnesty International, Asian  Human Rights Commission and a members  from the police department not below the rank  of Deputy Inspector General of police,  Pending hearing of the Rule restrain the  Respondents from proceeding with the  investigations of the cases filed against the  petitioners.  Upon hearing the parties and causes shown, if any, make the Rule absolute; Award costs to the petitioners; and Grant such other or further relief or reliefs to which the petitioners may be entitled in law and equity."

20. দরখাস্তকারীগণের রীট পিটিশনে বর্ণিত বর্ণনা অনুযায়ী অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি জনস্বার্থে দায়ের করা একটি মোকদ্দমা। দরখাস্তকারীগণের বিজ্ঞ আ্যাডভোকেট ড. কামাল হোসেন যুক্তিতর্ক উপস্থাপনকালে নিবেদন করেন যে, অত্র দরখাস্তটি জনস্বার্থে দায়ের করা একটি মামলা ।

He lastly submits that there is no bar to challenge the criminal proceedings under a writ jurisdiction but in that case, the petitioners have to challenge the concerned law to declare it ultra vires but in the instant case, no law has been challenged and in that view of the matter, the legal decisions referred to by the petitioners are not applicable to the present writ petition and in that view of the matter, this writ petition is not maintainable.

<u>48. I have gone through the applications filed by the petitioners under Article 102 of the Constitution and the materials annexed thereto. I have also considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the learned Attorney-General for Bangladesh. I have also considered their submissions to the best of my wit and wisdom. From the writ petition, it is noticeable that the petitioners have challenged the arbitrary and mala fide actions of the respondents committed through police officers under their control and supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and others and they have also prayed for direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in lodging of arbitrary, mala fide and fictitious cases against the petitioners and others. From the cause title and the prayer portion of the writ petition, it is clear that the petitioners have basically challenged the criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others under writ jurisdiction. The actions of police officers and the respondents are meant for criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others. It appears from the record that the petitioners are the accused of some cases of Paltan Model Police station and Mirpur Model Police station. It is evident from the record that the facts of some cases were published in different newspapers. On going through the FIR, it appears that some specific facts and offences narrating the chaotic situation in different roads of Dhaka City have been disclosed in those FIR. It may be stated that the facts and offences disclosed in the FIR are highly contentious and disputed question of fact. The truthfulness or falsehood of the allegations can be looked into by the investigating officers and the learned judges of the Court below at the time of framing charge and after recording evidence from the respective parties. The truthfulness and/or falsehood of the allegations cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. If there is any illegality or irregularity in the cases, that can be addressed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure if so challenged by the aggrieved person/s. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this writ petition is not maintainable in the eye of law. In the case of Samsunnahar Salam vs Mohammad Ohidur Rahman, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 232, it was held that:</u>

<u>"A writ Court cannot and should not decide any disputed question of fact which required evidence to be taken for settlement."</u>

49. In the case of TaeHung Packaging (BD) Ltd. vs Bangladesh reported in 18 BLC (AD) 2013 144, it was decided that:

"Even in presence of alternative remedy, the High Court Division can invoke the power of writ jurisdiction if the aggrieved person challenges the vires of a statute which requires interpretation of such statute."

50. It was further explicated in that decision that:

"The Court normally does not interfere with the investigation of a case where the offence has been disclosed in the FIR or complaint. The tendency of interference at the stage of investigation of a case is now on the rise which has not happened earlier even though it has repeatedly been pointed out that such assumption is not correct. The Courts should be weary of its possible consequence."

51. In the case of ACC vs Mehedi Hasan reported in 67 DLR (AD) 137, it was construed that:

"There is no scope for quashing a criminal proceeding under the writ-jurisdiction unless the vires of the law involved is challenged. The vires of the law involved in the case has not been challenged. Therefore, there is no scope for aggrandizement of jurisdiction of the High Court Division in quashing a criminal proceeding. Consequently, the High Court Division was not justified in quashing criminal cases in exercise of its power under Article 102 of the Constitution."

52. In the case of Begum Khaleda Zia vs Anti-Corruption Commission reported in 69 DLR (AD) 181, it was decided that:

"There is no scope for quashing a criminal proceeding under the writ jurisdiction unless the vires of the law involved is challenged. There is no scope for aggrandizement of jurisdiction of the High Court Division in quashing a criminal proceeding."

53. In the case of ACC vs Enayetur Rahman reported in 64 DLR (AD) 14, it was laid down that:

"This Court on repeated occasions argued that Article 102(2) of the Constitution is not meant to circumvent the statutory procedures. The High Court Division will not allow a litigant to invoke the extraordinary jurisdiction to be converted into Courts of appeal or revision. It is only where statutory remedies are entirely ill suited to meet the demands of extraordinary situations that is to say where vires of a statute is in question or where the determination is mala fide or where any action is taken by the executives in contravention of principles of natural justice or where the fundamental right of a citizen has been affected by an act or where the statute is intra vires but the action taken is without jurisdiction and the vindication of public justice require that recourse may be had to Article 102(2) of the Constitution."

54. In the case of ACC vs Shahidul Islam reported in 68 DLR (AD) 242, it was held that: "Challenging the proceedings of special cases, writ petition are not maintainable inasmuch as Code of Criminal Procedure provides efficacious remedy to get redress if one feels himself aggrieved due to initiation of such criminal proceedings."

55. In the case of Begum Khaleda Zia vs ACC, reported in 70 DLR (AD) 50, it was decided that:

"Where a person has an equally efficacious remedy, the High Court Division would not interfere with criminal proceeding in exercising extraordinary jurisdiction. Such powers are to be exercised in rare and exceptional cases."

56. It was further formulated in the aforesaid case that:

"Existence of alternative remedy is not an absolute bar to entertain writ petition by the High Court Division but to declare a criminal proceeding illegal, it is to be established that the Court acted without jurisdiction or the vires of the law is in question."

<u>57. It is evident from the FIR that the petitioners are the senior leaders of BNP and at the same time, they are made accused in different cases. So I have no hesitation to say that the petitioners are very interested persons in this writ petition and they have not come before this Court with clean hands. In view of the above, this writ petition cannot be considered as public interest litigation. 58. In this regard, the decision taken in the case of Dattaraj Nathuji Thaware vs State of Maharashtra, (2005) 1 SCC 590, 592-93 may be given as reference wherein it was spelt out that:</u>

<u>"A person acting bona fide and having sufficient interest in the proceeding of public interest litigation will alone have a locus standi and can approach the Court to wipe out violation of fundamental rights and genuine infraction of statutory provisions but not for personal gain or private profit or political motive or any oblique consideration."</u>

59. It was further decided in that case that:

"A writ petitioner who comes to the Court for relief in public interest must come not only with clean hands like any other writ petitioner but also with a clear heart, clean mind and clean objective."

<u>60. It is stated in the application that some cases have been filed against the dead person and the persons who were in abroad at the time of incidents and the very facts have been published in different newspapers. Basing on the aforesaid news, the petitioners have approached this Court challenging the actions of cases taken against them. It has been decided in a series of case laws that the disputed question of facts can be decided in writ jurisdiction. It is now well settled that newspaper reports cannot be admitted into evidence unless the correspondent of such a report comes to the witness box to vouchsafe in support of the report on oath. The aforesaid view finds support in the decision in the case of Osena Begum alias Babuler Ma vs State, reported in 55 DLR 299.</u>

61. I have also gone through the legal decisions referred to by the petitioners. The facts of those cases are quite different and distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case and do not match with the facts of the present case. Accordingly, those decisions are not applicable to the matter at hand. The petitioners could not produce a single case law which is apparently applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case at hand.

62. Having considered all the facts and circumstances of the case, the submissions of the respective parties, the propositions of law and the discussions made above, I do not find any merit in this application and accordingly, I am at one with the views and opinion of Mr Justice Md Ashraful Kamal.

63. In consequence thereof, this application under Article 102 filed by the petitioners is summarily rejected.

Let a copy of this judgment and order be communicated to the concerned respondents at once.
